items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: And I know that my teacher Darius Milhaud never had to check anything

ctx.x: At the piano? To see if—

Yes. To see if I’m close to right. And I know that my teacher Darius Milhaud never had to check anything and never had to be near a piano, and like a Mozart his mind worked, just some kind of perfection that God gave a few people. Stravinsky always wrote at the piano.
That’s interesting. The ideas that you’ve had in jazz, the polytonality and polyrhythmic, do you try to get those into your orchestral pieces also?

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Milhaud said, “After the war, you come study with me.”

ctx.x: You didn’t get a draft notice.
Yeah. So Milhaud said, “After the war, you come study with me.” That was great. I had something to always look forward to.
How familiar were you with his music? Had you heard his music at that point?
